- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for reversal.  
- If model shows a sharp spike in forecast (e.g., >+3% from prior period), reduce subsequent forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–68), model often overreacts; dampen forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.50, -0.00, +0.67), model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
